text:
maya: hey team :wave: first-week question — hitting a weird git-lfs auth failure on my mac (M2, macOS 13). regular git clone works but `git lfs pull` gives 401. i'm using 1Password ssh agent for SSH keys and mac keychain for HTTPS creds. anyone seen this with corp proxy + mac keychain?

tom: ugh that combo can be annoying. quick checks: `which git`, `git --version`, `git lfs env`, and check your proxy env vars. run: 
```
export | grep -i proxy
which git
git --version
git lfs env
```

maya: output snippets: 
```
$ which git
/usr/local/bin/git
$ git --version
git version 2.39.3
$ git lfs env
Endpoint=https://git.internal/acme/repo.git/info/lfs (auth=basic)
GIT_TRACE=1
```

jordan: couple things — 1) make sure the credential helper is set to osxkeychain for HTTPS: `git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`. 2) set GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1 and GIT_TRACE=1 to see the HTTP handshake details when `git lfs pull` fails.

sophia: also confirm whether the corporate proxy is rewriting auth headers. if `http_proxy` or `HTTPS_PROXY` is set in your shell or in the environment that your GUI/git process inherits, LFS calls may be going through a proxy that strips Authorization. try unsetting proxy for internal hosts with NO_PROXY or add the host to `no_proxy`. example: 
```
export NO_PROXY=git.internal,localhost,127.0.0.1
# or for zsh/bash in your dotfiles (~/.zshrc):
# export HTTPS_PROXY=http://corp-proxy:3128
# export NO_PROXY=git.internal
```

maya: ok i tried `git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain` (was set to `manager` previously) and re-ran `git lfs pull` with `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1 GIT_TRACE=1`. saw 407 Proxy Authentication Required earlier — looks like the proxy was intercepting.

tom: if it's 407 the proxy needs credentials. some folks set the keychain helper for the proxy auth or put proxy creds in a secure env var. but a safer fix is to route LFS traffic directly (NO_PROXY) for `git.internal` so it doesn't hit the proxy at all.

sophia: one more gotcha — if you installed git / git-lfs from Xcode CLT vs Homebrew you can get mismatched curl/ssl behavior. `brew reinstall git-lfs` and `git lfs install --force` helped a colleague. also check your PATH early in your dotfiles: asdf shims or other entries can change which git gets picked up.

maya: FYI `which git` is /usr/local/bin/git (brew). i ran `brew reinstall git-lfs` and `git lfs install --force`. then i updated my ~/.zshrc to export NO_PROXY for git.internal and restarted the terminal. `git lfs pull` now succeeds. :tada:

jordan: sweet. for the 1Password + ssh-agent side: if you're using their SSH agent integration make sure your agent is running in the same session as VS Code / terminal. `ssh-add -l` should list your keys. for mac keychain issues, `git credential-osxkeychain` can be used to manually erase stale creds: 
```
echo "protocol=https\nhost=git.internal" | git credential-osxkeychain erase
```

maya: thanks all — helped a lot. i added a short note to my onboarding dotfiles about NO_PROXY and brew git-lfs so future new-hires don't hit the same trap. :heart:

onboard-bot: Hey @maya — welcome again! If you want, drop a short step in the onboarding checklist at https://redwood.internal/onboarding/dev-setup and we'll add it to the central doc. :sparkles:
